chapters.title: The Deduction Board

lines.text: The choir sings again on Sunday. The warden's pew is empty. The hymnal stays open on the organ — to the page where Tobias Renner wrote the truth.
And in the hymnal, tucked between the pages, one more thing the police never logged: a small black envelope, sealed with a silver anchor.
Rain on the roof. Forty candles burning low. And at the bottom of the choir loft stairs, a man who will never conduct again.
Tobias Renner taught this city to sing. Tonight the cathedral is silent — and the silence is lying.
The police called it a fall. The hymnal on the organ disagrees. You are the detective the Cold Case Unit sends when the obvious answer is too tidy.

evidence.body: In Renner's hand: 'M.H. — the fund is short 40,000. Talk tonight.' The initials, the amount, and the meeting — written the day he died.

evidence.body: Two parallel drag marks cross the loft floor toward the stairs. The stairs themselves are clean. The body was moved after death.

premise: Tobias Renner, choirmaster of St. Anselm's Cathedral, is found dead at the foot of the choir loft stairs on a rainy Tuesday night. The parish calls it a tragic fall. His hymnal, open on the organ, says otherwise: in the margin, in his own hand, three words — 'the fund is short.' Someone in the choir wanted him silent, and the cathedral keeps its secrets in Latin.

solve.solutionHTML:
Marcus Hale met Tobias Renner in the choir loft at about 21:50, after Renner's 20:52 call summoned him to talk about the fund. When Renner showed him the figures, Hale struck him once with the brass candlestick, then dragged the body to the stairs and arranged the fall. He wiped the candlestick — but his print survived beneath the wipe — and he went back to the vestry, where the key log caught him leaving at 21:35. The motive is written in two places: Renner's hymnal, and the ledger's erased figures, 40,000 crowns rewritten to hide three years of theft through fake stonemason invoices.

No single clue convicts him. The print alone could be innocent — he polishes the brass daily. The ledger alone proves theft, not murder. The key log alone proves a lie, not a killing. Together, they leave no one else: only Hale knew the loft code, only Hale was seen at the stairs at 21:40, and only Hale had a reason to silence the one man who had done the sums.

I saw Marcus Hale near the loft stairs at about twenty to ten.
I was writing my sermon. The draft will show the time.

title: The Silent Choir

twists.body: Father Dominic admits he knew about the shortfall all along — and said nothing. If the parish's own priest covered for the theft, who else is protecting the warden? Or is the priest protecting himself: he was the only other person in the building with no witness that night.
twists.title: The priest's confession

twists.body: The safe holds a second set of books — and they show the theft is older and bigger than Renner knew: three years, not three months. Hale was not stealing to cover a mistake. He was stealing because he believed the cathedral owed him. And Renner was not the first person to notice — the first was the bookkeeper, who left the parish suddenly, two years ago, and never spoke again.
twists.title: The second set of books
